text_blocks.snippet: Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) originated in the mid-20th century. It was developed by Aaron T. Beck, a psychiatrist at the University of Pennsylvania, and Albert Ellis, a psychologist at Rutgers University.

Beck's work focused on the role of negative thoughts and beliefs in mental health problems, particularly depression. He observed that individuals with depression often had automatic negative thoughts that distorted their perceptions of reality. Ellis, on the other hand, emphasized the importance of irrational beliefs and developed a system of therapy called Rational Emotive Behavior Therapy (REBT).

Together, Beck and Ellis laid the foundation for CBT, which combines cognitive and behavioral techniques to help individuals identify, challenge, and modify negative thoughts and behaviors that contribute to mental health issues. CBT has since evolved and expanded to treat a wide range of disorders, including anxiety, substance use, and eating disorders.
